newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI chief sees interest rates rising.
newsitem.headline: India SBI chief sees interest rates rising.

text.p: Indian domestic lending rates will go up in the long term because of massive infrastructure demand for funds, the chief of India's biggest bank said on Friday.

State Bank of India (SBI) chairman Pandurang Kakodkar said investments in infrastructure like roads, ports, power and telecom would require 3,000 billion rupees which was not available through domestic savings.
"Our own savings rate is just 24 percent. It will not be enough at all to take care of the demand," he told a financial services conference.
"My projection is that long term interest rates will definitely go high," he said. "In the short term it will remain low." He did not say by how high or when the rates would go up.
Indian banks' prime lending rate currently is 14.5-15.5 percent against 16.5-17.0 percent a year ago.
Despite the decline in lending rates, bank loans to industry have failed to pick up due to a general slowdown in activity.
"Rate of growth of bank credit has increased nominally by one percent this year against a growth of 8.5 percent during the corresponding period last year," he said.
"There's a general talk of deceleration in the economy and all concerned ... are worried about it," he said.
Exports grew by only 9.9 percent during April-October 1996 against 24.4 percent in the year-ago period while imports rose 6.4 percent against 30.8 percent, Kakodkar said.
Excluding petroleum products import which jumped 43 percent, other imports comprising capital goods, chemicals and so on were down 1.6 percent, he said.
